original_test_intent: Verify the intended SUT's SMBIOS Type 24 Hardware Security structure and all defined security-status fields against the approved platform specification without changing security configuration.
original_method: Through protected read-only OS access, collect complete raw Type 24 output, bind it to SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS/parser identity, decode all status fields and compare them to the owner matrix, using any TPM/Secure Boot evidence only as explicitly scoped supplemental correlation.
manual_activity: The platform-security owner supplies expected Type 24 states and the allowed relationship to live security controls; an operator verifies target identity and protected access while automation performs the read-only comparison.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS and SMBIOS version
Expected Type 24 front-panel reset, administrator password, keyboard password and power-on password states
Policy for Enabled, Disabled, Not Implemented and Unknown values
Explicit scope of any supplemental TPM, Secure Boot or measured-boot correlation
Supported dmidecode/parser version and raw-field mapping
Protected credential/host verification, redaction and security-evidence storage
safety_requirements: Keep all collection read-only; do not enable, disable, enroll, clear or reset security features
Do not change BIOS passwords, TPM, Secure Boot, keys or BMC security configuration
Do not clear logs before relevant baseline evidence is retained
Never put passwords on the command line or disable host-key verification
Capture complete raw stdout/stderr and exit status, not a heading-only filter
Do not infer modern TPM/Secure Boot enforcement solely from legacy Type 24 fields
Stop on malformed, missing or ambiguous security data and require owner interpretation
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, expected Type 24 matrix and live-security coverage boundary
Collect complete raw `dmidecode --type 24` through protected access
Parse every defined status field and retain raw encodings
Optionally correlate approved read-only TPM/Secure Boot evidence without treating it as the same schema
Report comparison and no-mutation audit without issuing the verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Type 24 expected states and interpretation policy
Define whether supplemental live security evidence is required and how it is judged
Resolve Unknown/Not Implemented or metadata-versus-live discrepancies
Review protected evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the complete legacy Type 24 status byte into its four security fields, compare exact expected values and separately label any modern TPM/Secure Boot correlation so it cannot substitute for or be inferred from the SMBIOS record.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds full-field parsing, explicit enum policy, secure target binding and a boundary between legacy metadata and live enforcement.
